conviction_note: Nothing decisive and unpriced: the consensus EPS bar ($7.18) sits at or below the run-rate the raised FY guide implies, while the two programs that caused Q2's charges (GEM 63XL, SiAW) still have counterparty evidence of continuing trouble, and a promised 2027-28 cash-flow update is a guidance event of unknown sign; the findings sum to -0.9, while the scaled number is -0.18 because p_up is 48 on a 4.5-point absolute move. Beats on this name have been sold (Q2 beat-and-raise -2.2%, Q1 beat -7.0%), which keeps p_up near 50.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS $7.18 (7 analysts, range $7.04-7.32) and revenue ~$11.1bn, from https://tickerleague.com/companies/NOC/estimates (search snippet, 2026-10-19) and Benzinga $7.17-7.18 / $11.12bn https://www.benzinga.com/quote/noc/earnings ; two agreeing sources. Company guide FY2026 MTM-adj EPS $28.60-29.10, sales $43.75-44.25bn, segment OI $4.85-5.00bn, adj FCF $3.1-3.5bn (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001133421/000113342126000033/noc-06302026xearningsrelea.htm). H1 EPS 6.14+7.68 = 13.82, so guide midpoint implies H2 ~15.03; Q3 $7.18 leaves ~$7.85 for Q4. Year-ago Q3 2025 EPS $7.67. Company said H2 sales growth mid-to-high single digit, which on Q3 2025 ~$10.4bn puts Q3 near $11.0-11.2bn, i.e. on the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest ~1.7% of float (Benzinga sentiment page, snapshot 2026-09-08, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NOC/sentiment); FINRA 2026-07-15 settlement ~2.3m shares, 2.6 days to cover (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/noc/short-interest/); Equibles mid-Aug 1.62% of float, 2.2 days (https://equibles.com/stocks/noc/shortinterest). Not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. Baseline skew +1.87 vol points (mild put premium), put/call OI 1.07, priced lean 'balanced', event-implied move 3.86% (straddle 8.2% over 32 days). Stock +5.9% over 5 sessions into the print, -2.5% over 20, 33% below its 52-week high (record close $761.19 on 2026-03-02 per admiralmarkets).

findings.finding: ULA's Vulcan, the only customer of the GEM 63XL booster, had still not flown as of the KeepTrack deep dive published 2026-09-22 and reviewed 2026-10-17 (grounded since the 2026-02-12 USSF-87 nozzle anomaly, no return-to-flight date, Space Force moved the 18-launch SBST tranche to SpaceX on 2026-07-29), while NOC's Q2 call leaned on 'improved performance on GEM 63XL' for H2 Space sales and promised H2 Space margins 'north of 11%' after taking $71M (Q1) and $91M (Q2) of unfavorable EACs on the program; a third consecutive charge or lower GEM volume in Q3 is a live risk the guide does not include.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): EPS beat 12.6% and FY raise, stock -2.2% on the day as the GEM 63XL ($91M) and SiAW ($68M) charges took segment margin to 10.6%; Q1 2026 (2026-04-21) with the $71M GEM charge: -6.98%.
findings.why_not_priced: The grounding is public, but the Q3 consensus ($7.18) is built off a guide that assumed GEM recovery in H2; if the market were pricing another charge, Q3 estimates would sit below the guide-implied run-rate and the skew would be more than +1.87, and neither is the case. KeepTrack itself calls the $71M a floor, not a full cost estimate.
findings.independence: Q2 release quantifies the $91M EAC and the 'redesigned motors by end of year' plan: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001133421/000113342126000033/noc-06302026xearningsrelea.htm ; Spaceflight Now 2026-05-14 confirms the investigation still open after the April static fire: https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/05/14/ula-confirms-successful-solid-rocket-booster-test-as-vulcan-anomaly-investigation-continues/ . Net of the rest of the company: Space is ~$11bn of ~$44bn and Aeronautics (B-21, +13%) and Mission Systems (15.4% margin) were running ahead, so a GEM charge of the Q2 size (~$0.50 of EPS pre-tax ~ $90M/140m shares) can be absorbed elsewhere.

findings.finding: The Stand-in Attack Weapon charge ($68M in Q2) was tied to AARGM-ER test delays, and the AARGM-ER counterparty record since then points to more trouble rather than less: the Navy is withholding some payments because the missile is more than two years behind schedule (July 2026 report), DOT&E's FY25 report puts IOC at 1QFY27 against the Navy's stated September 2026 target, and FY27 US procurement is on a 'strategic pause'; the CEO said on the Q2 call 'we are not done the qualification until we are. There is risk.'
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the SiAW EAC was one of the two charges blamed for the -2.2% reaction to a beat-and-raise (https://parameter.io/northrop-grumman-noc-stock-drops-3-5-after-strong-q2-earnings-report/).
findings.why_not_priced: Payment withholding and the DOT&E slip sit in trade press and a test report, not in the earnings preview wire, which carries only consensus EPS. If priced, Defense Systems' H2 'over 11% excluding missile prime EACs' guide would be visibly discounted in estimates; consensus is not below the guide.
findings.independence: DOT&E FY2025 AARGM-ER report (IOC 1QFY27, test events delayed): https://www.dote.osd.mil/Portals/97/pub/reports/FY2025/navy/2025aargm-er.pdf ; TWZ on the strategic pause: https://www.twz.com/air/navy-still-pushing-to-field-new-air-defense-busting-missile-this-year-despite-strategic-pause . CEO quote from the Q2 transcript: https://www.webull.com/news/15265858912936960 . Net of the rest: Defense Systems is mid-to-high $8bn of ~$44bn, and SiAW is a development program inside it, so a charge is likely tens of millions.

findings.finding: The EPS bar is low against the company's own guide: Q3 consensus $7.18 is 6% below Q3 2025's $7.67, and the FY guide midpoint ($28.85) less H1 ($13.82) leaves $15.03 for H2, so the bar leaves ~$7.85 for Q4 with guided full-year ETR mid-14% and H2 segment margins guided 'low 11s'; NOC has beaten EPS in each of the last two quarters (Q1 $6.14 vs $6.06, Q2 $7.68 vs $6.82).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have been sold: Q2 2026 beat 12.6% -> -2.2%; Q1 2026 beat -> -6.98%; Q4 2025 (2026-01-27) +2.69%. The headline beat does not carry this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the beat cadence is well known. Q2's beat was flattered by a 6.3% tax rate (uncertain-tax remeasurement) and an equity-investment gain, so underlying Q2 was nearer ~$6.8, which is why the bar is not visibly 'easy' to the street. Small size.
findings.independence: Guide and H1 figures from the Q2 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001133421/000113342126000033/noc-06302026xearningsrelea.htm ; consensus from Benzinga: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/noc/earnings . Shares the Q2 8-K with finding 1.

findings.finding: Q3 brought sizeable munitions and strategic awards: two seven-year framework agreements worth over $3bn ($2bn PAC-3 solid rocket motors as second source, $1bn THAAD) announced 2026-08-03, a $111.4M Sentinel/GBSD contract modification dated 2026-09-26, and the company said on the Q2 call it expected NATO Triton (up to five aircraft) and a PAC-3 SRM production contract later this year; Q3 bookings and the multi-year munitions commentary are a modest positive against a FY book-to-bill guide of at least 1.25x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 posted a record 1.84x book-to-bill and $105bn backlog and the stock still fell 2.2%; bookings have not carried this stock on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: The agreements are public, but frameworks are not necessarily booked as net awards, and Q2's 1.84x is a tough comparison, so the read-through to Q3 net awards is uncertain; small size.
findings.independence: Breaking Defense on the PAC-3 second-source deal: https://breakingdefense.com/?p=91629 ; Sentinel assembly milestone 2026-09-15: https://thedefensepost.com/2026/09/15/usaf-northrop-grumman-sentinel-assembly/

findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call it would 'continue to refine' its 2027-2028 free cash flow outlook 'through this quarter' with further updates in Q3 and Q4, guiding capex to ~4.5% of sales in 2027-28 on top of $1.85bn in 2026 and a $2.5bn self-funded B-21 production investment, while buybacks have nearly stopped ($68M in H1 2026 vs $891M in H1 2025) under the January 2026 executive order restricting defense-contractor buybacks; a multi-year cash update at this print is a guidance event of uncertain sign that leans to the downside on the capex burden.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has moved this stock most: Q1 2025 guide cut -12.66%; Q2 2025 +9.41%. Cash-flow outlook changes specifically have no separate history in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: No preview found carries a 2027 FCF number or consensus; if the street had a firm view, 2027 FCF estimates and buyback assumptions would be on the wire, and they are not. Sign is genuinely uncertain, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: Buyback figure from the Q2 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001133421/000113342126000033/noc-06302026xearningsrelea.htm ; B-21 $2.5bn investment: https://breakingdefense.com/2026/04/northrop-to-invest-2-5b-to-hasten-b-21-production/ ; executive order: https://breakingdefense.com/2026/01/trump-warns-defense-ceos-to-beware-of-coming-limits-on-share-buybacks-salary/

findings.finding: FY2027 started under a continuing resolution to 2026-12-11 that keeps the Pentagon at FY26 levels and forbids new starts and new multiyear procurements, which can push Q4 award timing and color the 2027 commentary on the call; macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by NOC.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print turned on a CR; Q2 2026 call said 2027 growth is 'not dependent on significant supplemental or incremental funding above the base budget'.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; it is sector-wide and public. Filed small as a proxy.

outside_window.finding: Air Force decision on a larger B-21 program of record (100 to ~145 aircraft under review); CEO expected 'a conclusion by year-end'. It may be discussed on the call but the decision itself is not dated inside the window.
Vulcan return to flight (ULA target before end-2026, first flight likely Amazon Leo) would de-risk the GEM 63XL program.

baseline_tension: Mostly consistent with the baseline: a mild +1.87 put skew and a balanced lean match a small negative tilt from program-charge risk, while the +5.9% five-day run-up and this name's habit of selling beats argue against a positive reaction to an in-line or beat EPS.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): GEM 63XL -0.8 -> -0.6 and SiAW -0.5 -> -0.4, because Aeronautics and Mission Systems were running ahead and a charge of the Q2 size can be absorbed
Rule 1 (beats sold on this name): EPS-bar finding +0.3 -> +0.2 and p_up 47 -> 48
Rule 5 (macro proxy small): the CR finding -0.2 -> -0.1
Rule 6 (bar verified): two agreeing estimate sources ($7.18 TickerLeague, $7.17-7.18 Benzinga), so no cap; checked that the GEM/SiAW risks land outside what the guide assumed
Rule 7: short interest checked at ~1.7% of float, not crowded, so the negatives are not shrunk further for squeeze risk
Pessimism artefact noted: four negatives against two positives, all small; left as sized
